Authors: Gilani S.A.M.; Tantry A.; Askri S.; Sergio R.
Title: The role of broadband adoption/use in the survival and growth of food and drink micro-businesses in remote-rural Scotland
Abstract: The purpose of this article is to investigate the drivers and barriers to broadband adoption/use by food and drink micro-business owner-managers based in remote-rural Scotland. This study adopts a mixed methods approach consisting of 141 questionnaires involving rural restaurants, which is then followed by 42 semi-structured interviews with restaurant owners based in remote-rural Scotland. A Thematic analysis method offered the researchers simplicity as well as rigour to explore and arrange the retrieved data, which, in the opinion of the researchers, was necessary as it also offered flexibility to support the nature of this exploratory research study. The broadband adoption drivers of bookings, customer use, monetary transactions, and security [e.g. CCTV (Closed Circuit Television)], and barriers of lack of ISP selection and location of restaurants were highlighted as findings exclusive to this research study. The research also makes a key contribution by creating and developing the Broadband Adoption Framework (BAF) along with identifying broadband adoption/use drivers and barriers from the context of restaurant businesses based in remote-rural Scotland. The generalisability and representativeness of the sample in terms of different regions in remote-rural Scotland were a challenge due to a disproportionate sample under-representing some areas. Concerning remote-rural Scotland, recommendations are made for (1) food and drink business owner-managers and maximisation of the value added through broadband adoption/use; and (2) Scottish Government policy for ensuring equality of broadband access to ensure that rural-based businesses can effectively incorporate broadband into their operations. The findings from this research may better address the social exclusion and digital divide between urban and rural communities and businesses in Scotland. This study contributes to knowledge by identifying broadband adoption/use drivers and barriers exclusive to food and drink micro-businesses in remote-rural Scotland. However, some rural areas in Scotland were under-represented, and there was no primary insight gained from Scottish/UK government policymakers for broadband infrastructure in rural Scotland. It should be noted that the authors believe that in the case of future related studies, the validity, dependability and thoroughness of the findings can be enhanced by ensuring a more representative sample in terms of rurality and location. Additionally, the authors believe that results for drivers and barriers to broadband adoption/use may vary based on geography, sector, size and level of rurality for included businesses. © The Author(s) 2025.

Authors: Hensellek S.; Steigertahl L.; Mauer R.
Title: Non-linear and interaction effects of causation and effectuation on new venture performance: the role of ecosystem support
Abstract: Purpose – This paper investigates non-linear and interaction effects of causation and effectuation on entrepreneurial ventures’ performance, considering different levels of ecosystem support. Design/methodology/approach – Drawing on an ambidexterity perspective and recent research on causation and effectuation, we theorize curvilinear and interaction effects of causation and effectuation on venture performance that depend on the level of ecosystem support (i.e. from the government, business associations and accelerators/incubators). We empirically test our hypothesized model with a cross-country dataset of 861 European entrepreneurial ventures using multivariate regression analysis. Findings – We find that causation has a J-shaped relationship with venture performance. Furthermore, the interaction of causation and effectuation has a positive effect on performance. Both effects are stronger in environments with low levels of ecosystem support. Originality/value – This research delivers novel insights into individual and interaction effects of two entrepreneurial decision-making logics (i.e. causation and effectuation) that were often investigated as opposing logics. The results contribute to the literature on causation, effectuation and venture performance and answer calls for more contextualization of entrepreneurship research by investigating the differential role of ecosystem support in the effectiveness of both decision-making logics. Additionally, it provides practical advice for policymakers, entrepreneurs and other ecosystem actors. © 2025 Simon Hensellek, Lisa Steigertahl and René Mauer

Authors: Kim H.; Shin H.H.; Yoon H.; Shin H.
Title: Why travelers prefer humans over artificial intelligence (AI): Developing and testing an AI aversion model in tourism
Abstract: As tourism businesses increasingly adopt artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance traveler decision-making, a persistent reluctance to rely on AI-generated recommendations has emerged as a critical barrier. This research addresses this gap by developing and validating an AI aversion model that identifies the factors driving traveler resistance to AI-generated recommendations. Using a mixed-methods approach, this research uncovered five core drivers rooted in the perceived absence of human nature attributes: lived experience, emotional engagement, contextual understanding, domain specific knowledge, and proactive engagement in communication. Twenty-three items were developed and validated in a multicultural context. Additionally, we revealed that individual differences (i.e., rational vs. emotional personalities) play a moderating role, which can offer a way to mitigate the negative impacts of AI. The findings offer theoretical contributions by enriching the understanding of AI aversion and repositioning technology resistance through a human lens and extending practical implications for firms aiming to integrate AI effectively. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Thi Cam Ha V.; Chau Nguyen T.; Thi Thu Pham T.; Ramsawak R.
Title: Foreign direct investments and the wage gap dynamics: The labor market and absorptive capacity effects
Abstract: This paper investigates the impact of foreign direct investment (FDI) presence on the wage gap between domestic-FDI firms and how the effect varies depending on the domestic firms’ absorptive capacity and labor share in the labor market. Using a ten-year firm-level panel with over 400,000 observations, the study controls for firm and industry-specific effects and differences in the local business environment. Findings reveal that while increased FDI presence within an industry (horizontal FDI) widens the domestic-FDI wage gap, increased presence of FDI in the vertical value chain (vertical FDI) reduces it. Our results show that both horizontal and vertical FDI exert significant effects on domestic wages through the labor market channel. While productivity spillovers from foreign firms do translate into higher wages for workers in domestic firms, thereby reducing the wage gap, the magnitude of this effect varies with the share of labor in domestic firms in the sector. Notably, the negative impact of horizontal FDI on the domestic–FDI wage gap diminishes in domestic firms with greater absorptive capacity, and higher absorptive capacity amplifies the positive wage-equalizing effect of vertical FDI, further narrowing the wage gap. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Al-Ahmed H.; Alshaketheep K.; Al-Okaily M.; Kinana S.B.
Title: Sustainability education in business schools: From responsible management identity to sustainable marketing competency
Abstract: Although there is increasing adoption of sustainability in business education, there is a paucity of empirical studies that describe the process of sustainability education transferring to domain specific managerial skills. Based on the Transformative Learning Theory, Experiential Learning Theory, and Social Identity Theory, this paper constructs and empirically validates an integrative model, which connects exposure to sustainability education with perceived sustainable marketing competency via the mediating variable of responsible management identity. The model also investigates the moderating relationship of the intensity of experiential learning and the Teaching Approach Quality. 1154 business students in Jordan, Palestine, and Saudi Arabia were used to gather data and analyzed through PLS-SEM. The results show that sustainability education is strongly associated with responsible management identity, which is strongly associated with perceived sustainable marketing competency. This relationship is partially explained by responsible management identity. In addition, higher levels of experiential learning intensity and Teaching Approach Quality are associated with a stronger relationship between sustainability education exposure and responsible management identity, as well as stronger conditional indirect associations with perceived competency development. Multigroup analysis indicates structural invariance across the three countries. The research contributes to the responsible management education literature by demonstrating that sustainability education is associated not only with what students know, but also with how they perceive themselves as future managers, with responsible management identity playing a central role in the development of perceived sustainable marketing competency. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Frey P.; Gnisa F.
Title: Co-determination as an anticipatory practice? German works councils and the democratisation of the future
Abstract: We explore the role that works councils can play in promoting inclusive and democratic innovation processes in companies by democratising anticipatory practices. Drawing on interviews with 33 experts from 13 German organisations with particularly well-developed co-determination practices, we examine how works councils envision their companies’ futures and shape organisational transformations in the interests of employees and, potentially, society more broadly. Across manufacturing, public administration, and retail, we identify complementary forms of strategic intervention and employee participation. Works councils analyse societal and industry trends, develop visions for digital transformation, and introduce technology demonstrators to stimulate debate among employees about future working environments. In doing so, they broaden the range and diversity of stakeholders involved in corporate anticipatory practices and governance. We then discuss the conditions that have enabled these rare pioneers to develop the epistemic capacities required for more inclusive forms of anticipation. Business decisions, and with them the most consequential anticipatory practices, are usually monopolised by corporate management and owners. We therefore discuss structural reforms, including amendments to the German Works Constitution Act, that could strengthen workers’ voices in corporate governance. Such reforms could democratise anticipatory practices, support more socially and environmentally sustainable innovation, and contribute to better societal outcomes. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Ma B.; Zhou L.; Mu Y.; Chen Y.; Zhang J.
Title: Impact of CEO perceived dominance on corporate financial performance: an empirical study based on facial feature extraction via deep learning
Abstract: Perceived dominance, which can be formed on the basis of the facial features of a chief executive officer (CEO), can affect the behavior of other firm members (i.e., other executives and subordinates) and impact corporate outcomes. However, a consensus has yet to be reached on the association between CEO perceived dominance and corporate financial performance owing to limitations in sample representativeness, measurement errors, and empirical strategies of previous studies. This study investigates the impact of CEO perceived dominance on corporate financial performance through facial feature extraction via deep learning, which can provide robust and causal insights from a large dataset spanning a long time period of 30 years. Furthermore, this study explores the mechanism of the impact of CEO perceived dominance from the perspective of information flow and sharing by investigating the moderating effects of CEOs’ nonsalary compensation, board size, and the number of business segments. The results indicate that the degree of CEO perceived dominance is negatively associated with corporate financial performance and that a CEO’s high nonsalary compensation, large board size, and large number of business segments can attenuate the negative association. Our findings can deepen the theoretical understanding of the impact of CEO perceived dominance on corporate financial performance and provide managerial implications for the decision-making of investors. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Zhu R.; Tang C.; Ge P.
Title: ESG news sentiment and firm viability: evidence from external governance shocks
Abstract: Firm viability is a fundamental objective of corporate governance, yet it is increasingly influenced by external governance pressures arising from ESG-related information disclosed by various external stakeholders. ESG news sentiment represents a salient form of such external governance shocks. Using a comprehensive sample of Chinese A-share listed firms, we find that negative ESG news sentiment significantly undermines firm viability. This adverse effect is particularly pronounced among manufacturing firms, non-high-polluting industries, small firms, and non-state-owned enterprises. Mechanism analysis reveals that ESG news sentiment diminishes firm viability by suppressing financial support and damaging business operations. Moreover, stronger ESG performance amplifies the adverse effect of negative ESG news sentiment on firm viability, suggesting that firms with better ESG reputations are more sensitive to adverse external governance shocks. These findings highlight the important role of external information environments in shaping firm viability and provide new insights into how ESG-related information influences corporate sustainability. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Authors: Nesterova K.; Annenkov A.; Brynzylo A.
Title: Management of large shopping and entertainment centres under martial law
Abstract: The purpose of this article was to examine the operations of shopping and entertainment centres (SECs) under crisis conditions. To achieve this goal, management methods for SECs were analysed, and a survey of managers of major Ukrainian SECs was conducted. The study revealed significant challenges faced by large SECs in Ukraine from 24 February 2022 to 2024. The primary consequences of the invasion included reduced economic activity, declining footfall, disrupted supply chains, and increased security threats to staff and visitors. As the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) fell by 28.8% and unemployment rose to 25%, this negatively impacted the operational activities of shopping centres, leading to decreased profits and heightened financial instability. The survey of SEC managers identified key strategies for overcoming these challenges, including reducing rental rates for tenants, implementing humanitarian initiatives, adapting business models, and establishing financial, material, and personnel reserves to ensure operational resilience. The study also demonstrated that implementing security measures, involving employees in decision-making, improving communication efficiency, and enhancing coordination with partners could serve as effective stabilisation factors. Business model adaptation, particularly debt restructuring and the introduction of new lease terms, may help mitigate operational risks and maintain basic operational stability under crisis conditions. The findings indicated that the resilience of SECs during wartime and their post-war recovery depend on the effective integration of adaptive business models and security measures. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

Authors: Li Y.
Title: Government roles in legalizing China’s digital business environment: evidence from Beijing, Shanghai, and Chongqing
Abstract: The digital business environment has become a focal point of global competition. As the world’s second-largest economy, China’s digital economy has a huge scale, and its exploration of institutional innovation and governance has enlightening significance for the international community. However, existing research mainly focuses on traditional business environments and lacks a systematic analysis of the role of government in digital business environments. This study aims to clarify the specific role, path differences, and influencing factors of local governments in the legalization of the digital business environment. Selecting Beijing, Shanghai, and Chongqing as samples to conduct semi-structured interviews and qualitative comparative research on relevant government departments. Research has found that, firstly, although the government has achieved results in optimizing the approval process and shortening the start-up time of enterprises, there are still regional differences; Secondly, Beijing and Shanghai have entered a further stage of improving the quality of public services and ensuring the rule of law, while Chongqing is still in the stage of basic reform; Thirdly, the disadvantages of location, talent, and finance in non-first tier cities constrain the development of their digital business environment. Overall, China is gradually narrowing the gap with international best practices such as B-READY and still needs to continue efforts in cross-border rule integration, legal transparency, and service-oriented government. This study points out the diverse paths of local governments in legalizing the digital business environment, and also provides institutional references for other developing countries. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Rajabi M.M.; Linnenluecke M.; Han J.; Smith T.
Title: How big is the carbon bubble really?
Abstract: We examine how major U.S.-listed fossil fuel firms respond to discrete climate policy signals, including annual United Nations climate summits and four major policy announcements, by estimating market-implied valuations under business as usual (BAU) and policy-adjusted scenarios and the associated carbon bubble. Using data from the stock and options markets, we infer the value of the carbon bubble as the difference between the observed market price and policy-adjusted valuations. This study finds that the carbon bubble corresponds to 5.5% of current firm value, or approximately $99.3 billion, suggesting that markets perceive moderate downside risk from regulatory and policy shifts. Firm-specific analyses, including Exxon Mobil, indicate that climate policy events can materially influence risk distributions, with 5% value-at-risk estimates under BAU scenarios ranging from 12% to 45% under policy-adjusted scenarios. These findings highlight that financial markets systematically incorporate climate policy developments into firm valuations while indicating the overall resilience of fossil fuel assets under both BAU and policy-adjusted scenarios. © 2026 The Authors. Authors: Ałaszewski A.
Title: mOkazje Zakupy: How mBank is redefining the future of digital banking through the shopping experience
Abstract: This paper explores mBank’s groundbreaking initiative mOkazje Zakupy, which integrates a full-featured shopping platform directly into its mobile banking app. Launched in partnership with Morele.net, the platform represents a strategic shift in digital banking, transforming the app from a transactional tool into a lifestyle companion. By leveraging its trusted brand, rich customer data and advanced personalisation engine, mBank delivers a seamless, secure and highly contextual e-commerce experience. The initiative reflects broader trends in platform banking and embedded finance, positioning mBank as a leader in redefining customer engagement in the European financial sector. The paper highlights the technological, operational and strategic dimensions of the project, emphasising its scalability, regulatory compliance and potential to reshape the role of banks in the digital economy. Beyond its technical execution, mOkazje Zakupy reflects a broader strategic vision: to increase customer engagement, reduce churn and unlock new monetisation pathways. The initiative aligns with global trends in embedded finance and platform banking, offering a European benchmark for how banks can evolve into digital ecosystems. Authors: Panda D.; Parida V.; Frishammar J.
Title: When industrial companies implement circular business models, what do they really do?
Abstract: Purpose – Implementing circular business models (CBMs) in industry is promising yet difficult. Prior research has largely focused on identifying barriers to CBM adoption and the enablers needed to overcome them. However, addressing barriers alone is insufficient, as circularity must ultimately be embedded in companies’ routine-based practices to become operational and scalable. Existing practice-oriented studies remain limited and tend to examine isolated aspects of CBMs, such as value creation, value delivery or value capture, rather than how these dimensions are pursued together. This study aims to address this gap by synthesizing how industrial companies implement CBMs through phase-based practices that span business model dimensions. Design/methodology/approach – The authors conducted a three-stage review (identification–screening–eligibility) of academic and gray literature, ending with 87 studies included. Using qualitative content analysis, the authors coded circular practices and their underlying activities and applied the Gioia methodology to visualize them. The study grounds in the Swedish industrial context, given its early and coordinated adoption of circular economy policies and strategies. Findings – The findings reveal a three-phased CBM implementation process: designing, developing, and scaling. In the design phase, companies explore circular value logics, build internal capabilities, and renew ecosystem partnerships. The development phase involves testing circular concepts, transforming organizational processes, and launching new revenue models. Finally, the scaling phase focuses on market expansion and digital integration to enhance circular operations. Originality/value – This study advances CBM literature by identifying business practices and underlying activities that outline how industrial companies implement CBMs in practice. It structures these practices into a phased framework along with specific actions and key considerations for each phase. Finally, it shows how value creation, delivery and capture are activated differentially across implementation phases. © 2026 Debadrita Panda, Vinit Parida and Johan Frishammar.

Authors: Wang W.; Hong Z.; Lian Z.; Cui J.; Liu W.
Title: Government report ESG emphasis and firms’ ESG disclosure
Abstract: This study examines the impact of government report environmental, social, and governance (ESG) emphasis on firms’ ESG disclosures. Relying on a textual analysis of municipal government reports in China, we find that government report governance emphasis significantly encourages firms to enhance their ESG disclosures, whereas environmental and social emphasis do not yield significant effects. Consequently, the overall impact of government report ESG emphasis on ESG disclosure is positive but statistically insignificant. Notably, these findings remain robust even after addressing potential endogeneity and using alternative model specifications. Moreover, the impact of government report ESG emphasis varies by firm ownership, geographical region, and ESG ratings, with differences observed across the three ESG categories. We also explore the specific actions firms undertake in response to government report ESG emphasis. These empirical insights highlight the crucial role of government narratives in shaping corporate reporting behavior and suggest that policymakers can leverage these narratives to promote sustainable business practices and improve ESG transparency. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Authors: Amato A.; Machado M.R.; Moreira J.L.R.
Title: Leveraging early warning systems and customer segmentation to identify business opportunities in the financial industry
Abstract: Early Warning Systems (EWS) are essential in the dynamic information management environments of banks and financial institutions to monitor credit portfolios and detect early indicators of financial distress. The literature shows that EWS typically focus on identifying negative indicators, lacking research on positive metrics. Banks and financial institutions can enhance their operations by utilising artificial intelligence to incorporate automated Customer Segmentation (CS) techniques to identify positive indicators, such as up-selling opportunities and enhance information systems management. This study explores how integrating EWS into a new CS model can reveal possible business opportunities in commercial credit portfolios, with an emphasis on segment orientation, identifiability, and actionability. We utilise a dataset from a major European commercial bank to experiment our approach for combining EWS with CS to provide information management solutions. We utilised K-Means and DBSCAN clustering techniques with EWS indicators, in addition to Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction, to efficiently categorise the client base. We conducted risk–reward and risk exposure evaluations and analyses to improve clients’ understanding of health. The assessment of clustering outcomes demonstrated that PCA is superior in improving the compactness and distinctiveness of clusters. Our research provides valuable insights into strategic risk monitoring by integrating EWS and CS. This allows banks and financial institutions to customise their services for various client groups, enhancing strategic decision-making and potentially boosting profitability. © 2026 The Author(s).

Authors: Pérez-Moure H.; Lampón J.F.; Velando-Rodríguez M.-E.; Rodriguez-Comesaña L.
Title: Transforming B2B service innovation – the path toward new digital-intensive business through entrepreneurship
Abstract: Purpose – This study aims to explain the areas of opportunity for entrepreneurship offered by digitalization and proposes strategic recommendations for entrepreneurs and firms offering B2B services in the digital economy. Design/methodology/approach – Exploratory research is used to analyze how digitalization is affecting B2B services entrepreneurship in the mobility industry. A mixed methodology combining 4 in-depth interviews and a Q-survey with 30 participants was used. The information obtained was processed using qualitative and quantitative analysis tools to identify areas of opportunity and suggest actions to improve the possibilities of entrepreneurship. Findings – This study identifies artificial intelligence (AI)-driven business models, data and resource management and selective investment filtering as the most promising paths in B2B services, while suggesting that sustainability is not as critical as previously assumed. The findings also indicate that servitization and personalization have varying levels of impact, with personalization being less effective in B2B than previously expected. Moreover, the role of individual entrepreneurial alertness is diminishing, giving way to collective learning, technological alternation and strong networking effects as key drivers of success in digital-intensive B2B environments, providing a new perspective on entrepreneurial alertness. Research limitations/implications – The findings emphasize that B2B firms should adopt a modular transition approach to digitalization, enabling step-by-step implementation rather than radical transformation. The research also suggests that not all digital investments are equally viable, with AI-powered logistics, smart supply chains and data-driven platforms outperforming traditional models such as vehicle hire and taxi booking services. The shift from individual to collective learning and strategic networking is essential for capturing and leveraging entrepreneurial opportunities in a rapidly evolving digital landscape. Entrepreneurs and business leaders should prioritize building robust ecosystems, leveraging industry collaborations and integrating emerging technologies into their business models. Originality/value – This study makes several novel contributions. First, it introduces new theoretical insights on entrepreneurial alertness, emphasizing its transition from an individual-driven process to a collective and technology-enabled phenomenon. Second, it provides a comprehensive synthesis and valuation of digital-intensive business models, ranking them according to their strategic viability in B2B contexts. Finally, this study identifies the key characteristics shaping entrepreneurial success in digital B2B markets, emphasizing the importance of network-based learning, adaptive ecosystems and the integration of AI-driven decision-making. © 2026 Hugo Pérez-Moure, Jesús F. Lampón, Maria-Elena Velando-Rodríguez and Lorenzo Rodriguez-Comesaña.

Authors: Arango-Pastrana C.; Arango-Espinal E.; Osorio-Andrade C.
Title: From crime to search engine: how crime predicts the search for security products?
Abstract: This study analyzes how property crime rates influence public interest in online security solutions in Colombia between 2010 and 2025. Using a quantitative approach, a Vector Autoregressive Model with Exogenous Variables (VARX) incorporated official National Police crime statistics as exogenous variables and Google Trends indicators for “Surveillance,” “Insurance,” and “Private Security” as endogenous variables. Results show that vehicle theft most strongly increases searches across all categories, business theft mainly drives interest in private security, and residential theft boosts insurance-related searches. These findings demonstrate that digital traces serve as real-time indicators of perceived insecurity, offering valuable insights for strategic business decisions and public policy. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

Authors: Shi Y.; Yang X.
Title: Virtual reality stimulating customer creativity in product co-development
Abstract: The creativity of customers is crucial in determining their effective participation in product development and co-creation. This paper investigates how to stimulate customer creativity in product co-development through VR technology. An empirical study was conducted using a questionnaire survey within the theoretical framework of technological mediation. The results demonstrate that VR’s technological embodiment immerses users in realistic virtual environments, enhancing perceived realism and, in turn, fostering customer creativity. Moreover, the possession–self link serves as a mediator between perceived realism and customer creativity. Additionally, self-extension tendency moderates both the effect of technological embodiment on perceived realism and the impact of perceived realism on the possession–self link. This study contributes to the literature on technological mediation theory, consumer creativity, and VR while offering valuable insights for VR designers and businesses. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Steinmetz J.; Pronin E.
Title: The objectivity illusion and perceptions of online reviews
Abstract: Research on online reviews has identified reviewer- and review-related factors that impact persuasiveness. We add to this literature by investigating reviewers’ as well as readers’ perspectives on a given review. We find that reviewers’ “objectivity illusion”—the belief that their opinions are objective, i.e., reviewer objectivism—adversely impacts readers’ reactions to their online reviews. In two studies and one supplemental study, we find for positive as well as negative reviews that reviewers habitually high in objectivism see their reviews as more persuasive and are more willing to share them, although readers evaluate them as less persuasive because they find objectivist reviewers less likable. These studies demonstrate that reviewers who write less persuasive reviews are most likely to share them, which holds implications for businesses seeking to improve review persuasiveness. © The Author(s) 2025.

Authors: Azad Honari N.; Dawson A.; Chadwick I.C.
Title: Mothering legitimacy: The role of mothers in supporting daughters’ legitimacy as successors in an adverse societal context
Abstract: The aim of this research is to investigate the role of mothers in supporting the legitimacy of their daughters as family business successors in societal contexts that are unfavorable to women. While, in general, daughters may still face greater challenges than sons in establishing legitimacy as business leaders and successors in family businesses, this struggle is further exacerbated in societal contexts where women do not have same economic rights as men and face legal barriers preventing their full economic participation. In these contexts, mothers may play a critical part in fostering their daughters’ legitimacy, supporting them in key leadership roles in the family business. Through qualitative methodology, and choosing Iran as our research context, we contribute to family business literature by illustrating the role of mothers in the legitimacy formation of daughters who have become family business successors. Based on our analysis, we propose a typology of mothers – as champion, unseen mentor, unsupportive or low influence – based on two aggregate dimensions relating to mothers’ influence in empowering daughters and mothers’ position in business or society. Our findings offer a nuanced understanding of the role of mothers in shaping their daughters’ legitimacy as leaders in family businesses, despite an unfavorable societal context. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Chaity N.S.; Masud A.A.; Emon M.; Islam M.F.; Neumann A.
Title: AI's sustainable edge: How green supply chain management and innovative behavior bridge capability to performance
Abstract: This study investigates how Artificial Intelligence Capability (AIC) might drive Sustainable Performance (SP) in businesses. It concentrates on the pivotal roles of Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM), and Green Innovative Work Behavior (GIWB) as mediate that guides the impact of AIC to the results of sustainability. Moreover, the paper will examine the role of Agile Leadership (AL) in enhancing the effect of AIC on GHRM, GSCM, and GIWB by highlighting its role as a key mediator in the AI-sustainability relationship. The research is an empirical study and convenience survey study and has a sample size of 455 representatives of the various types of companies in developing country. The research was carried out through the online survey. The data were analyzed through structural equation modeling (SEM). This study determined that GHRM and GSCM mediate the association between AIC and GIWB to a significant degree. Moreover, we have found that the connection between AIC and SP is rather mediated by GHRM, GSCM, and GIWB. Also, the findings indicated that AL has a significant moderating effect on the association between AIC to GHRM, GSCM, and GIWB. This study gives new insights into the interaction of AI potentials, green HRM, green SCM and green innovative behavior on long-term performance, in which GHRM, GSCM, and GIWB have significant mediating roles. It also demonstrates the way agile leadership manages such interactions, which develops our understanding of AI-based workplace sustainability. © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd. Authors: O'Brien M.P.; Daniels M.; Ryan A.
Title: Beyond the lecture: Creative and innovative pedagogies in management education – An integrative conceptual review
Abstract: Management education has been criticised for over-reliance on transmission-oriented pedagogies poorly suited to developing the competences contemporary business graduates require. The case for moving beyond the lecture is strengthened by generative artificial intelligence, which performs the analytical and reproductive tasks underpinning conventional assessment, shifting educational value toward judgement, situated decision-making, and reflection. This integrative conceptual review of creative and innovative pedagogies draws on literature published principally between 2013 and 2026, organising the field into six clusters: experiential and simulation-based learning; game-based and gamified approaches; arts-based methods; design-based pedagogies; problem-based learning; and student-generated multimodal artefacts. For each cluster it examines theoretical foundations, evidence strength, and implementation challenges, distinguishing outcomes with stronger evidence (engagement, motivation) from those with weaker evidence (durable transfer). Three cross-cutting themes are identified: the centrality of learner agency, the neglect of structured reflection, and institutional conservatism as a barrier to change. The review contributes a typology of creative pedagogy organised by locus of creation and mode of engagement, which is used to make explicit the trade-offs each configuration entails and where institutional conservatism constrains change, together with implications for programme design, assessment and facilitation, and a research agenda spanning longitudinal measurement, equity, programme-level integration, and generative AI. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Drummond M.; Cronshaw S.; Pickles M.
Title: The academic experience in using gamification to facilitate business and management learning: A UK case study
Abstract: The use of gamification in Higher Education has increased over the last decade, with notable dominance of gamification use within the subject area of business and management. Studies have previously proven that gamification can engage and motivate students in their learning, however there is still some apprehension about its use among staff. Academic staff from a UK Higher Education Institution were interviewed about their experience of using digital gamification in their classroom. Transcripts were thematically analysed with findings identifying that gamification can be time-consuming and staff are often the primary source of technical support should any issues surrounding system navigability occur. The results can help academic staff consider their use of gamification, informing their assessment design when adopting gamified approaches as well as developers of gamified products, who can draw upon the findings to aid their product development. The findings further highlight a need for developers to ensure system functionality is intuitive enough that academic staff do not need provide guidance for functional needs and that their role remains in support of academic theory and evaluation of student experience. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Deng Z.; Li P.P.; Larsen M.M.; Zhou A.J.
Title: Toward a pendulum framework of firm internationalization
Abstract: Driven by escalating geopolitical tensions, trade conflicts, the pandemic, and regional crises, traditional efficiency-centric liberal globalization has evolved into a “new” pattern of globalization that prioritizes resilience, security, and geopolitical alignment. Multinational enterprises (MNEs) are rapidly reshaping global operations via reshoring, nearshoring, and friendshoring, redrawing the landscape of international business. This Special Issue explores how MNEs adapt to and shape a new pattern of globalization, covering three core themes: (1) geographical reconfigurations; (2) MNE strategic options; and (3) advances in international business theory. Integrating nine selected papers, this editorial proposes a pendulum framework for firm internationalization, depicting MNEs' dynamic oscillation between overseas expansion and home retreat to balance efficiency and security at the global scale. The framework also reveals an upward spiral in capability upgrades amid strategic shifts and delineates salient boundary conditions. It concludes with future research directions on internationalization dynamism, multi-polar geo-strategies, and capability development in the fractured global economic order. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Sopian N.M.; Pitchay A.A.; Bawa N.K.
Title: Bibliometric insights into innovation capability: Intellectual foundations and emerging themes
Abstract: Innovation capability has emerged as a critical determinant of organisational competitiveness, yet the literature remains fragmented across diverse theoretical perspectives and contexts. This study aims to consolidate existing knowledge by conducting the first comprehensive bibliometric analysis of innovation capability research.The dataset was extracted from the Scopus database on 31st March 2026, yielding 1720 peer-reviewed journal articles indexed under Business, Management and Accounting. After preprocessing, performance analysis was undertaken to examine publication trends, influential authors, institutions, countries, and journals. Science mapping techniques, using VOSviewer, were applied to visualize co-authorship, co-citation, and keyword co-occurrence networks, enabling both descriptive and structural insights.The number of publications shows a clear upward trend over time, with a sharp increase after 2015 and a peak around 2025. Influential contributions stem primarily from Elsevier journals and leading institutions in Finland, China, and Malaysia, while collaboration networks remain fragmented. The intellectual structure is anchored in dynamic capabilities, absorptive capacity, and the resource-based view, with thematic evolution moving from internal knowledge integration toward digitalization, sustainability, and resilience. Emerging hotspots include artificial intelligence, Industry 5.0, and green innovation, though underexplored geographies and methodological diversity persist. This study represents the first large-scale bibliometric mapping of innovation capability, providing an integrative overview of its intellectual foundations, conceptual structures, and thematic evolution. By highlighting gaps in geographical coverage, sectoral applications, and methodological approaches, it sets an agenda for future research and offers actionable insights for managers and policymakers seeking to strengthen innovation capability in turbulent environments. © 2026 China Science Publishing and Media Ltd.

Authors: Suh W.; Atlas S.A.
Title: Time and risk preferences among generative AI systems
Abstract: This research examines the choices and values of generative AI systems, such as ChatGPT by OpenAI, by adapting classic behavioral protocols to elicit their time and risk preferences. These systems generally, though not always, revealed greater patience and more risk-averse behavioral patterns compared to human populations. While reminiscent of human decision-making, the preferences exhibited by AI followed systematic patterns that differed across AI systems. These findings highlight the importance of treating AI as a distinct decision agent, which can help improve AI selection, support more effective human-AI collaboration, and offer new ways to simulate behavioral patterns for consumer behavior research and business applications. © 2026 Elsevier Inc. Authors: Parra Torres J.M.; Torres Castillo C.; Carlier S.I.
Title: Beyond standalone ethics courses: The role of institutional ethos in a business school
Abstract: Following major corporate scandals such as Enron and the subprime crisis, debates about the mission of business schools and their responsibility to cultivate ethical leadership tend to intensify. However, Parra et al. (2022) show that, despite extensive scholarship on the topic, institutional responses to external pressure are often superficial and fragmented, falling short of the structural reforms required for robust ethical formation. This article presents a single-case study of a Colombian private business school to examine how the alignment between institutional identity/mission and the input–process–output design of its educational system can strengthen ethical formation. The case is analytically valuable because it captures a coherent, mission-driven model operating within a competitive environment shaped by regulations, accreditations, market demands, and rankings—conditions common to many business schools yet underexplored in Latin American contexts. Methodologically, we conduct a document-based case study drawing on institutional sources (mission and vision statements, program outlines and evaluations, and accreditation reports). The study contributes to the literature on management education and ethics by, first, proposing a conceptual model that holistically links institutional policies and practices to the effectiveness of ethics education; and second, applying this model to a concrete institutional practice to illuminate how specific educational variables interact and with what implications for learners. Findings indicate that tight identity–design alignment can deepen ethical learning while remaining responsive to external pressures; however, they also reveal vulnerabilities to misalignment and potential trade-offs in faculty socialization and adaptability. We discuss implications for designing system-level strategies that move beyond isolated pedagogical initiatives. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Jeon J.; Sivakumar K.; Athaide G.A.; Raj S.P.
Title: Artificial intelligence at the intersection of innovation and marketing: A conceptual model and research propositions
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the theory and practice of innovation and marketing, yet its deployment at their intersection remains only partially understood. Existing literature has not thoroughly examined which AI capabilities (analytical, generative) are more appropriate during different stages of the new product development (NPD) process, how a core marketing factor, customer involvement, conditions the outcomes of these capabilities, or how AI-related risks and governance mechanisms shape NPD performance across stages. This study addresses these gaps by proposing a novel conceptual framework that links the two distinct AI capability types to specific NPD stages, examines how customer involvement moderates the relationship between AI capabilities and NPD outcomes, integrates AI hallucination risk as a formal boundary condition differentiating the failure modes of AI capabilities across stages, and extends the framework to NPD governance mechanisms including gate evaluations, feedback loops, and cross-functional coordination. The paper contributes to research and practice by (1) offering a set of propositions regarding AI's role at the intersection of innovation and marketing, (2) providing theoretically derived guidance for managers on deploying AI capabilities during NPD while recognizing the marketing imperative of customer involvement, and (3) outlining a future research agenda on AI-enabled innovation which is of crucial importance for the future of business. Collectively, the paper advances a more theoretically rigorous and practically relevant understanding of AI's transformative role in innovation and marketing. © 2026 The Authors

Authors: Hruby J.
Title: Reflection quality and psychological safety as mechanisms of development in virtual management education
Abstract: This study examines the mechanisms linking behavioral participation in virtual management education to developmental learning outcomes. Drawing on experiential learning theory (ELT), this study investigates whether reflection quality mediates the relationship between behavioral participation and student development and whether team psychological safety moderates the participation–reflection relationship. Data were collected from an eight-week multicultural virtual leadership program involving 74 business students working in nine multicultural teams. To reduce common method concerns, this study integrated six independent sources of evidence: instructor activity logs, coded reflection reports, pre- and post-program competency surveys, psychological safety ratings, peer evaluations, and instructor-assessed team-performance scores. The findings indicate that higher behavioral participation is associated with deeper reflective responses. Reflection quality is more consistently associated with gains in cultural intelligence (CQ) and global leadership competency than participation alone. Furthermore, the relationship between participation and reflection is stronger in teams characterized by higher psychological safety, highlighting the importance of supportive learning environments in fostering reflective practices. Because reflection depth and post-program outcomes were assessed at the same measurement occasion, the mediation findings are interpreted as theory-consistent associative evidence rather than causal proof. Overall, the results are consistent with a sociocognitive extension of ELT, in which experiential learning is shaped not only by individual cognitive processing but also by the interpersonal safety of the team environment. For management educators, the findings emphasize three design priorities: systematic monitoring of behavioral participation, scaffolding and assessing reflection quality, and intentionally cultivating psychologically safe learning environments to enhance developmental outcomes in virtual management education. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Patwary A.K.; Li L.; Parvez O.; Cobanoglu C.; Supina S.
Title: Collective identity, organizational commitment, and environmental conservation: An integrated model for U.S. hotels
Abstract: The study tests a new approach to linking collective environmental identity (CEI) and high organizational identity (HOI) to environmental conservation through affective, normative, and continuance commitment. We used PLS-SEM version 4 to examine these connections using cross-sectional data from hotel workers across the US. The results show that collective environmental identity is linked to affective, normative, and continuance commitment, and that a strong organizational identity further strengthens these commitments. Affective, normative, and continuance commitment also shape the link between employees' environmental conservation and collective environmental identity. These results show how important it is to have dedicated workers who support sustainable practices. Companies, especially those in the rapidly growing US hotel industry, can use this framework to embed sustainability in their business plans by engaging and empowering employees. This study contributes to the hospitality literature by demonstrating how identity-based commitments lead to concrete actions that benefit the environment. This has not been examined in the context of hotel employees before. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Alam S.S.
Title: Willingness to buy at AI powered retail stores in Saudi Arabia: Empirical study
Abstract: The study builds on established theories, including the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Trust Theory, and Perceived Risk Theory, to investigate how personalization, interactivity, and cultural factors impact AI trust and how this trust mediates willingness to buy, particularly in the context of performance risk. Utilizing a cross-sectional quantitative research design, data were collected from 410 respondents. The findings reveal that personalization and interactivity significantly enhance AI trust, which, in turn, positively influences willingness to buy. Performance risk is shown to have a dual role, sometimes acting as a deterrent and other times enhancing willingness to buy when the AI systems are perceived as innovative. Cultural dimensions also significantly shape willingness to buy, although they have a more direct impact on willingness to buy rather than on trust formation. These insights provide theoretical advancements in understanding AI adoption and practical implications for businesses looking to optimize AI-powered platforms. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Institute of Applied Informatics at University of Leipzig 2025.

Authors: Xu G.; Kang N.; Zhou X.
Title: More than regulation: How policy mixes shape innovation ecosystems in digital transformation
Abstract: The era of digital transformation drives the continuous restructuring of innovation ecosystems, challenging regulators to move beyond conventional regulations to address market and system failures. Although policy mixes are essential to address these challenges and promote innovation ecosystems, the efficacy of specific policy mix characteristics remains underexplored. This study develops a conceptual model to explore the mechanisms through which policy mix characteristics affect firm innovation in the digital transformation era. Specifically, we conceptualize policy mix coordination across three dimensions: temporal (policy stability over time), horizontal (policy similarity across regions), and vertical (policy coherence and complementarity between central and local governments). Firm innovation is examined through firms' technological and business positions within the innovation ecosystem. We conduct an empirical study of Chinese listed companies (2001-2021), employing machine learning techniques to identify policy themes, multi-source heterogeneous network analysis to measure firm innovation, and panel regression to test hypotheses. Results show that temporal and horizontal coordination stimulate firms' technological positions but inhibit business positions, whereas vertical coordination significantly enhances firms' technological positions within innovation ecosystems. These findings contribute to policy mix theory by incorporating a thematic lens and offer insights into recasting regulators' role as strategic coordinators in cultivating innovation ecosystems during digital transformation. © 2026 Elsevier Inc.

Authors: Bordbar Y.; Chang W.; King B.E.M.
Title: When anger delivers: leader anger expression and employee performance in hospitality
Abstract: Purpose – The expression of anger is a much-observed phenomenon in hospitality workplaces. Most previous research has associated anger with destructive outcomes and devoted less attention to its constructive potential. This study aims to investigate both the positive and negative consequences of leader anger expression, along with the moderating role of ethical leadership. Drawing on the emotions as social information (EASI) model, it examines how leader expressions of anger and ethical leadership jointly shape employee job crafting, performance and emotional responses. Design/methodology/approach – Data were collected from 296 employees in the US hospitality and tourism sector using a two-wave time-lagged survey design. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was deployed to test the hypothesized relationships. Findings – It is shown that there is a direct increase in job crafting because of both controlled and outward leader anger, thereby enhancing task performance. Controlled anger reduces employee anger and indirectly improves job crafting and performance, whereas outward anger increases employee anger, weakening its constructive effects. Ethical leadership weakens the calming effect of controlled anger though strengthens the positive relationship between outward anger and employee anger. Practical implications – As they engage in the ongoing pursuit of improvements in business performance, leaders should engage proactively in managing anger and reducing its incidence among employees. Ethical leaders should be aware that their displays of emotion may have unintended consequences if they provoke employee anger. Originality/value – This study provides theoretical contributions to research on leadership and emotions in hospitality and tourism by advancing a context-dependent understanding of leader expressions of anger. It offers practical insights for managers on how ethical leadership affects employees’ emotional perceptions, underlining the merit of adapting leadership styles to specific contexts. © 2026 Younes Bordbar, Wen Chang and Brian Edward Melville King.

Authors: Tang Y.; Huang L.; Zou L.
Title: An understanding of sustainable transformational leadership and innovation ambidexterity: the mediating roles of social and psychological capital
Abstract: This study investigates the complex interrelationships among sustainable transformational leadership (STL), psychological capital (PSY), social capital (SOC), and sustainable innovation ambidexterity (SIA) within China’s manufacturing sector. Drawing upon social capital theory and positive organizational behavior frameworks, the research developed and empirically tested a comprehensive model examining direct and mediating relationships among these constructs. Data were collected from 520 employees across various hierarchical levels in Chinese manufacturing organizations. Utilizing partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), the findings reveal that STL is significantly associated with SIA, SOC, and PSY. Furthermore, SOC significantly predicts both PSY and SIA, while PSY is significantly associated with SIA. The study contributes to existing literature by holistically understanding how leadership practices foster sustainable innovation capabilities through social and psychological mechanisms. The findings provide valuable insights for manufacturing organizations seeking to enhance their sustainable innovation capabilities while maintaining operational efficiency in an increasingly sustainability-focused business environment. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Maung L.O.; Chaturvedi A.
Title: AI–Blockchain Adoption in Low-Cost Airlines: A Diffusion-Based Model for Disruption Management
Abstract: The airline industry is increasingly adopting the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain to enhance operational resilience and disruption management. While conceptual discussions are growing, there remains a lack of validated measurement studies examining the determinants, adoption dynamics, and integration of AI–blockchain systems, particularly in low-cost carriers (LCCs). To address this gap, this study develops and validates a diffusion-based measurement model of AI–blockchain adoption and its relationship with disruption management effectiveness. Grounded in an integrated Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory and Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) framework, the study proposes nine latent constructs encompassing technological, organizational, and environmental factors, along with post-adoption dimensions including adoption rate and integration quality. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 300 aviation professionals, including airline operations specialists, consultants, technology vendors, and academics. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was used to evaluate the measurement model. The results demonstrate satisfactory factor loadings, composite reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity, supporting the robustness of the proposed model. The findings confirm that the identified constructs provide a rigorous framework for understanding the adoption and integration of AI–blockchain technologies in airline operations. This study contributes to the transportation business and management literature by advancing AI–blockchain adoption beyond initial acceptance and emphasizing the role of integration quality in enhancing disruption management effectiveness. The proposed framework provides a foundation for future research examining structural relationships and performance outcomes of emerging digital technologies in aviation. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Kumari A.; Aggarwal A.; Srivastava P.
Title: Bridging gaps to excellence: a multi-case study of OD interventions in Indian automotive MSMEs
Abstract: The aim of the present study is to identify organisational development (OD) intervention as a driver for achieving organisational excellence (OE) in micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSME) in India. The paper identifies the OE challenges faced by the selected MSME firms. Furthermore, the study investigates the types of OD interventions applied in these firms to manage the OE challenges. In this vein, the actual impact of OD interventions in minimizing the OE challenges is also explored. A cross-case methodology based on qualitative exploratory research design was employed involving 33 semi-structured interviews with management and staffs of MSME firms from the automotive industry in India. Axial coding and triangulation was used to analyse the responses. The study found five OE challenges of selected firms: “financial literacy,” “corporate structure and business environment,” “knowledge and skills,” “techniques and functioning styles,” and “resource utilization”. The results explained the success of OD interventions in reducing these OE Challenges. A five-level framework is proposed to reflect the pertinent organisational areas where OD interventions can be introduced to help MSMEs to attain OE. The paper contributes to the HRM literature on organisational development. The proposed interventions recommend efficient management, continuous improvement, and shared leadership. In practice, the role of training and development as well as leadership development is emphasised, and these can be executed by embedding OD interventions in the relevant OE areas. This study is the first of its kind to use multi case approach, apply OD interventions and explore it’s impact in achieving organisational excellence within the Indian MSME automotive industry. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Aghimien D.; Aghimien E.I.; Aigbavboa C.O.; Aliu J.O.; Oke A.E.; Chan D.W.M.
Title: Strategies for enhancing construction digitalisation: a machine learning-based sensitivity analysis
Abstract: Purpose – To achieve digitalisation, construction organisations need strategies to help align existing business structures with emerging digital technologies. To this end, this paper presents the findings of an assessment of the strategies required for construction digitalisation using South Africa as a point of reference. Design/methodology/approach – The study adopted a mixed-method design using a Delphi and questionnaire survey, while the critical strategies for digital construction were identified using three different machine learning (ML)-based sensitivity analyses. Findings – The study, through factor analysis, found five major groups of strategies: (1) understanding the construction market, (2) creating a digital culture, (3) technology deployment and assessment, (4) communication management and (5) finance. However, the three ML-based sensitivity analyses all revealed that technology deployment and assessment, as well as understanding the construction market, are the two most important strategies for construction digitalisation in South Africa. Originality/value – The paper offers practical guidelines for construction organisations to be digitalised. It also offers methodological contributions to using ML in survey studies within construction. Authors: Nguyen K.M.; Dang M.T.; Nguyen Thi L.D.; Nguyen H.G.; Nguyen Hoang Hung T.; Phan Thi Minh D.; Nguyen N.T.
Title: Fostering employees' adoption of machine learning-enabled technologies in asset pricing
Abstract: Purpose – This research aims to explore how financial professionals perceive and apply machine learning (ML) in asset pricing, identifying key determinants of its adoption by examining the role of institutional pressures, individual and organizational factors. In addition, the study examines the moderating roles of technology interconnectivity and technology interoperability in the association between employees' ML adoption intention and actual usage behavior. Design/methodology/approach – Using a quantitative approach, data were gathered from 689 financial professionals in Vietnam through an online survey targeting those with experience or knowledge in asset pricing. The research model was analyzed using structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4 software. Findings – The results indicate that ML knowledge, perceived cognitive capabilities, personal innovativeness and leadership vision positively influence employees' intention to adopt ML. However, contrary to expectations, concerns about job displacement and organizational innovativeness were found to negatively affect ML adoption. Moreover, adoption intention strongly predicts the actual use of ML in asset pricing practices. Originality/value – This study pioneered insights into how individual and organizational factors, such as leadership vision and cognitive abilities, shape ML adoption in finance. It highlights the interplay between digital transformation, employee perceptions and organizational culture in emerging markets. Policymakers and businesses can use these findings to drive innovation and enhance competitiveness in the ML-driven financial sector. © Khoi Minh Nguyen, Minh Tran Dang, Linh Dan Nguyen Thi, Han Gia Nguyen, Thanh Nguyen Hoang Hung, Dung Phan Thi Minh and Ngan Thanh Nguyen

Authors: Marrone T.; Cantone L.; Basile V.; Testa P.; Cantone G.F.
Title: Beyond promotions: business model innovation in everyday low pricing grocery
Abstract: Purpose – This paper seeks to conceptualise an integrated, dynamic, everyday low-price (EDLP) retail business model (EDLP-RBM) and understand how retailers revitalise their EDLP business model in today’s hypercompetitive environment. Design/methodology/approach – The study is based on an in-depth, longitudinal case study of EDLP retailers, employing a multi-case study methodology. The qualitative approach adopts an exploratory grounded theory perspective to build an interpretive theory for EDLP-RBM and BMI. Findings – The paper proposes an extended representation of the EDLP-RBM, highlighting the interlocking elements that collectively renew the BM to create, capture and deliver value in a competitive context characterised by significant discontinuities for the retailers. Research limitations/implications – The main limitation is related to the qualitative nature of the research, which reduces the opportunity for generalising the results. Practical implications – The case studies reveal that the BMI can serve as a redefinition of the value proposition currently offered within the industry (i.e. conventional EDLP, HILO and discount retailing) and how the operating model delivers it. Originality/value – The study puts in evidence how leading Italian EDLP retailers innovatively and dynamically (re)combine different conceptual frameworks of BMs, such as their strategic variables, by experimenting with new ways to renew their competitive advantage to create and capture value. © 2025 Terersa Marrone, Luigi Cantone, Vincenzo Basile, Pierpaolo Testa and Giuseppe Fabio Cantone

Authors: Lin Q.; He L.
Title: Is competition good or bad for employee innovation? Examining the double-edged sword effect of team and individual responses
Abstract: Amid an increasingly competitive environment, fostering innovation among employees has emerged as a central concern for both academia and the business community. Drawing upon the conservation of resources (COR) theory, this study develops a multi-level framework to examine the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions of competitive psychological climate (CPC) on employees' innovative work behavior. By gathering data from 386 hotel employees and their leaders spanning 60 teams throughout four provinces along China's southeastern coast, the results indicated that CPC facilitated employees' innovative work behavior by increasing team cooperative orientation (i.e., resource-gain pathway); simultaneously, it inhibited innovative work behavior by eliciting workplace anxiety (i.e., resource-depletion pathway). Furthermore, psychological capital buffered the resource-depletion pathway, while error tolerance reinforced the resource-gain pathway. The results advance theoretical insight into CPC's dual influence mechanism and offer practical guidance for motivating employees to innovate in the highly competitive hospitality sector. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Yu T.; Dai J.; Chen X.; Wang C.
Title: From information evaluation to technology use: Generative AI adoption in Chinese business schools
Abstract: This study investigates the adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) among Chinese business school students by integrating the Information Adoption Model (IAM) and the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Specifically, it examines how argument quality, source credibility, perceived ease of use (PEU), and expertise shape students' perceived usefulness (PU), behavioral intention (BI), and actual use of GenAI. Using survey data collected from 672 business school students and analyzed through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), the results indicate that PEU, argument quality, and source credibility significantly enhance PU, which in turn positively influences students’ intention to adopt GenAI. Behavioral intention demonstrates strong predictive power for actual use, reaffirming the intention–behavior linkage central to TAM. The findings further reveal that expertise positively moderates the relationship between argument quality and PU, suggesting that more knowledgeable students are better equipped to evaluate the substantive strength of AI-generated outputs. Multigroup analyses show that gender, educational level, and prior AI experience significantly moderate key structural relationships. Female students place greater emphasis on PEU when forming usefulness perceptions, while students with prior AI experience rely more heavily on argument quality in evaluating PU. Moreover, female students, postgraduate students, and those with prior AI experience exhibit stronger intention–actual use relationships compared to male students, undergraduates, and students without prior AI experience, respectively. By integrating IAM and TAM in the GenAI context, this study provides a theoretically grounded explanation of how information evaluation processes translate into technology adoption behaviors. Practically, the findings offer actionable insights for policymakers and educators seeking to promote responsible and effective GenAI adoption, highlighting the importance of tailoring strategies to different student demographics and experience levels. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Olsson V.; Jalali A.
Title: An empirical study on the effectiveness of decision trees and decision tables for source-based decision validation
Abstract: Effective decision-making requires models that are both understandable to users and capable of representing complex logic. Decision trees and decision tables are widely used graphical notations, yet prior research reports inconsistent findings on their relative effectiveness. This study addresses that gap through a controlled experiment with 69 business experts from a national education agency, comparing the comprehensibility and user acceptance of both notations. Drawing on Cognitive Fit Theory and the Technology Acceptance Model, it examines task accuracy alongside perceived ease of use and usefulness in source-based validation tasks. Decision tables are perceived as significantly more useful than decision trees, whereas perceived ease of use does not differ between the notations. Task accuracy is moderately positively correlated with perceived ease of use. Overall, both notations support decision validation, but decision tables’ higher perceived usefulness provides a meaningful basis for favoring them when user acceptance is a priority in source-based validation contexts. Authors: Trueba-Castañeda L.; Somohano-Rodríguez F.M.; Torre-Olmo B.
Title: Assessing the role of financial risk attitudes in small and medium-sized enterprises’ digitalization and sustainability investment decisions
Abstract: In today’s complex business environment, the financial risk attitudes of the managers of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) shape their approach to opportunities and challenges. A proactive stance leads to strategic decisions, especially in terms of funding, innovation, and long-term growth. This study examines how financial risk attitudes impact investments in digitalization and sustainability. Digitalization boosts efficiency and competitiveness, whereas sustainability ensures long-term viability. An analysis of 400 Spanish SMEs using a structural equation model reveals that SMEs with positive financial risk attitudes are more likely to invest in these areas than are those with negative attitudes. Access to finance plays a crucial mediating role in this relationship, enabling bolder, forward-looking decisions. Improved financial access strengthens the link between risk attitudes and strategic growth, enhancing business performance. The study underscores the importance of fostering a risk-aware yet opportunity-driven mindset among SME managers to improve decision-making and secure a competitive edge in an evolving market. © The Author(s) 2026.

Authors: Shen S.; Yang S.; Jiang Y.
Title: Enhancing communication competence and managerial skills through virtual reality based experiential learning in management education
Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) has emerged as a promising pedagogical modality in higher management education, offering immersive, risk-free environments that simulate the complexity of real-world organizational interactions. This study investigates whether, and to what extent, VR-based experiential learning is associated with students' communication competence and managerial self-efficacy, drawing on Kolb's Experiential Learning Theory and Bandura's Social Cognitive Theory. Using a cross-sectional survey design complemented by platform-generated usage logs, we analyzed survey and behavioral data from 412 postgraduate and undergraduate management students across three program types at a research-intensive business school. Ordinary least squares regression served as the primary analysis, supplemented by instrumental-variable estimation (IV/2SLS), generalized method of moments (GMM), and propensity score matching to address potential endogeneity and selection bias. Bootstrap mediation analyses indicated that experiential learning depth and reflective practice partially mediate the associations between VR intensity parameters and both outcomes. Heterogeneity analyses revealed stronger associations among executive-education participants and where instructor facilitation quality was high. Findings were robust to alternative specifications and sample-trimming procedures. The study contributes a multi-method framework for integrating immersive technology into business-school curricula and offers actionable recommendations for curriculum designers, institutional administrators, and educational-technology policymakers. © 2026

Authors: Mukherjee A.; Mukherjee A.; Mateen A.; Deva Prasad M.
Title: Navigating the legitimacy landscape of the e-commerce ecosystem: A case study from India
Abstract: E-commerce retailing became a part of people’s everyday lives rapidly, but how such ventures attained legitimacy is rarely explored in the literature. Utilising the theoretical lenses of regulatory entrepreneurship, legitimacy, and platform power, we analyse how leading e-commerce firm Amazon paved their way towards legitimation and business expansion in India, an emerging economy, amidst a shifting regulatory landscape. Our in-depth case study of Amazon India from 2013 to 2023 culminates into a process model depicting organisational strategy and agility through three phases we named as exploration, construction, and tunnelling. The supply chain acts as a lever to utilise regulatory entrepreneurship strategies which can aid in rapid market expansion reinforced by the firm’s platform power. Firms need to utilise first mover advantages, collaborate with government, set industry standards, incorporate subtle cultural hints, and cast a positive influence by providing socio-economic empowerment alongside superior customer experience to attain pragmatic, cognitive, and sociopolitical legitimacy. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Institute of Applied Informatics at University of Leipzig 2026.

Authors: Van Khoi T.; Khanh P.X.
Title: From Green Skills to Sustainable Business Development: The Role of Vocational Education, Green Business Strategy and Environmental Innovation
Abstract: Sustainable business development (SBD) has been the global requirement due to uncertainty of economic and environmental conditions around the globe. Thus, the present article investigates the green business strategies and environmental innovation role of the green dynamic capabilities (DC) and SBD in plastic waste recycling companies in Vietnam. The study also examines the mediating role of green DC among green business strategies, environmental innovation, and SBD as well as investigates the moderating role of vocational education among green business strategies, environmental innovation, and green DC. The study selected the employees of the waste recycling companies in Vietnam and collected the data from the respondents using survey questionnaires. The study also checks the data reliability using the measurement model and association among variables using the structural model through smart-PLS. The outcomes revealed that the green business strategies and environmental innovation have a positive association with green DC and SBD. The results also exposed that the green DC significantly mediates among green business strategies, environmental innovation, and SBD and that vocational education significantly moderates among green business strategies, environmental innovation, and green DC.
